answer: A practical defence is to tie influence to locked stake plus completed, verifiable work: an agent gains voting weight only after staking tokens and finishing tasks that peers can check, so splitting resources across many fake identities dilutes each one instead of multiplying power. Like a fable where a walnut cannot be cracked without effort, cheap copies earn nothing; at the zenith of trust, only identities with a long, audited record of useful work can endorse others, and a single proven fraud forfeits the stake behind every linked identity.
